title: Simply Majestic
summary: Use a checking bishop move to keep the pawn alive, then sacrifice the promoted queen to build a mating cage.

nodes.question: Should White trade the pawns immediately?
nodes.explanation: White has Kd5, Be3 and g6 against Kf8, e7 and h7. Trading g6 for h7 leaves the pawn exposed; a bishop check changes the king’s route.

branches.title: Give up the queen to force the king into the cage
commentary: Reconstruct the complete six-piece starting board. Black’s two pawns are essential to the final mating cage.
Bh6+ checks along the h6–f8 diagonal, moving the bishop before the pawns are exchanged.
Kg8 approaches the promotion square rather than retreating toward the center.
g7 prevents ...hxg6 from removing White’s only pawn and keeps Black’s king tied to the corner.
Kf7 leaves the corner, apparently preparing to stop promotion with the king.
g8=Q+ promotes with check and deliberately offers the new queen to the king.
Kxg8 accepts the queen. White has only a bishop left, but Black’s own pawns will help close the escape squares.
Ke6 controls d7, e7 and f7 and blocks the e-pawn on its starting square. The bishop controls f8 and g7, leaving the king only h8.
Kh8 is the only legal move: the king cannot leave through f7, f8 or g7, and the e-pawn is blocked by Ke6.
Kf7 maintains control of e7, f8 and g8 but releases the e-pawn. Black now has to spend a pawn move.
e5 is the source’s selected double pawn advance. The king remains trapped in the corner.
Bg7# is actual mate. Kf7 protects Bg7 and covers g8, while Black’s own h7 pawn blocks h7.
branches.explanation: Bg7# is actual mate. Kf7 protects Bg7 and covers g8, while Black’s own h7 pawn blocks h7.

branches.title: Capture h7 before checking
commentary: Compare the source’s immediate pawn trade, before the bishop changes the black king’s route.
gxh7 gives up the forced win: the new h-pawn cannot be protected on its promotion square.
Kg7 attacks h7 and controls h8, preparing to capture a promoted piece.
h8=Q+ is the illustrated attempt to promote anyway; its check does not save the queen.
Kxh8 removes White’s last pawn. King and bishop against king and pawn is exactly drawn here.
branches.explanation: Kxh8 removes White’s last pawn. King and bishop against king and pawn is exactly drawn here.

branches.title: Advance the e-pawn instead of escaping
commentary: Follow the same checking preparation, then compare Black’s illustrated pawn advance.
Bh6+ changes the black king’s route before the pawn tension is resolved.
Kg8 remains near the pawn, hoping to prevent promotion.
g7 keeps the white pawn and restricts the king’s escape squares.
e5 tries to make progress with the spare pawn rather than moving Kf7.
Ke6 supports the approach toward f7 and the cornered king. White keeps the exact win.
e4 advances the pawn again. The lesson stops at this checked winning position; the remaining bishop collection and promotion are source context.
branches.explanation: e4 advances the pawn again. The lesson stops at this checked winning position; the remaining bishop collection and promotion are source context.

exercises.prompt: How can a lone bishop still help deliver mate?
exercises.answer: Black’s h7 pawn blocks its own king. White’s king and bishop can coordinate with that obstruction after the queen sacrifice; the lesson does not claim that bishop and king alone can mate a bare king.

exercises.prompt: Why does the checking move come before the pawn push?
exercises.answer: Bh6+ changes the black king’s route before g7 preserves the pawn. Immediate gxh7 allows ...Kg7 and removal of the promoted queen.

startContext: The complete six-piece starting board is visually reconstructed. Three selected source branches compare the queen sacrifice, an immediate drawn pawn trade, and Black’s e-pawn alternative. Every encoded position is checked exactly; these are selected variations rather than an exhaustive defense tree.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
